body_html:
The big idea

Multiply or divide as if there were no decimal point. Then put the point back in the right place. An estimate tells you where it goes.

Multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1,000

Each place is 10 times the place to its right. So multiplying by 10 moves every digit one place left, and the decimal point moves one place right.

Multiply or divide byThe point movesExample
× 101 place right3.45 × 10 = 34.5
× 1002 places right0.67 × 100 = 67
× 1,0003 places right2.8 × 1,000 = 2,800
÷ 10 (or × 0.1)1 place left45.6 ÷ 10 = 4.56
÷ 100 (or × 0.01)2 places left73 ÷ 100 = 0.73

Fill empty places with zeros: 2.8 × 1,000 = 2,800, and 8 × 0.01 = 0.08.

Decimal × whole number

With bigger numbers, multiply as whole numbers, then count the decimal places.

Example

What is 6 × 1.25?

Estimate: 6 × 1 = 6, so a bit more than 6. 6 × 125 = 750. 1.25 has 2 decimal places: 7.50.

Answer: 7.5

Decimal × decimal

On a hundredths grid, shade 0.3 of the columns and 0.4 of the rows. The overlap is the product.

Count the decimal places in both factors. The product has that many.

ProblemWhole numbersDecimal placesProduct
0.3 × 0.43 × 4 = 121 + 1 = 20.12
2.3 × 1.423 × 14 = 3221 + 1 = 23.22
0.5 × 0.125 × 12 = 601 + 2 = 30.060 = 0.06

Dividing decimals

To divide by a whole number, divide as usual and put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend.

To divide by a decimal, first make the divisor a whole number. Multiply both numbers by 10 (or 100). The answer does not change.

Example

What is 4.8 ÷ 0.6?

Multiply both by 10: 4.8 ÷ 0.6 = 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Check: 8 × 0.6 = 4.8.

Answer: 8

Estimate to check

Round to easy numbers first. 2.9 × 4.1 is about 3 × 4 = 12, so 11.89 makes sense and 118.9 does not. Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes the answer smaller; dividing by a number less than 1 makes it bigger.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.3 × 0.4 = 1.2Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so 0.12
3.45 × 10 = 3.450Move the point: 34.5. Adding a zero at the end does not change the value
Thinking 8 × 0.5 is more than 8Multiplying by less than 1 makes it smaller: 8 × 0.5 = 4
8.16 ÷ 4 = 2.4Write 0 when the divisor does not fit: 2.04
4.8 ÷ 0.6 = 4.8 ÷ 6Move the point in both numbers: 48 ÷ 6 = 8

faq.q: How do you multiply decimals in 5th grade?
faq.a: Multiply as if there were no decimal points, then count the decimal places in both factors and give the product that many. For 2.3 × 1.4: 23 × 14 = 322, and 1 + 1 = 2 places gives 3.22.

faq.q: How do you divide a decimal by a decimal?
faq.a: Multiply both numbers by 10 or 100 so the divisor becomes a whole number, then divide. 4.8 ÷ 0.6 = 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

faq.q: Why does multiplying by a decimal make a number smaller?
faq.a: Multiplying by a number less than 1 takes only part of the number. 8 × 0.5 is half of 8, which is 4.

Multiplying by 1,000 makes every digit 1,000 times as big, so each digit moves 3 places to the left. That means the decimal point moves 3 places to the right: 0.36 → 360. Write zeros to fill the empty places. Check: the answer must be bigger than 0.36.

Dividing by 10 makes every digit 10 times smaller, so each digit moves 1 place to the right. That means the decimal point moves 1 place to the left: 45.6 → 4.56. Check: the answer must be smaller than 45.6.

Dividing by 10 makes every digit 10 times smaller, so each digit moves 1 place to the right. That means the decimal point moves 1 place to the left: 7 → 0.7. Write a 0 in the ones place. Check: the answer must be smaller than 7.

Dividing by 100 makes every digit 100 times smaller, so each digit moves 2 places to the right. That means the decimal point moves 2 places to the left: 73 → 0.73. Write a 0 in the ones place. Check: the answer must be smaller than 73.

Dividing by 1,000 makes every digit 1,000 times smaller, so each digit moves 3 places to the right. That means the decimal point moves 3 places to the left: 1,250 → 1.25. Check: the answer must be smaller than 1,250.

Multiplying by 0.1 is the same as dividing by 10, so each digit moves 1 place to the right. That means the decimal point moves 1 place to the left: 36 → 3.6. Check: the answer must be smaller than 36.

Multiplying by 0.01 is the same as dividing by 100, so each digit moves 2 places to the right. That means the decimal point moves 2 places to the left: 250 → 2.5. Check: the answer must be smaller than 250.

items.q: To find 0.52 × 1,000, how does the decimal point move?
items.e: 1,000 has 3 zeros, and multiplying makes the number bigger, so the point moves 3 places to the right: 0.52 → 520. Write a zero to fill the empty place.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 4.7 × ☐ = 470
items.e: 4.7 → 470: the point moved 2 places to the right (4.7 → 47 → 470). Moving 2 places right is multiplying by 100. Check: 4.7 × 100 = 470.

items.q: Multiplying by 0.1 is the same as …
items.e: 0.1 is 1 tenth. Taking 1 tenth of a number is dividing by 10: 36 × 0.1 = 3.6 = 36 ÷ 10. (Dividing by 0.1 does the opposite: it is the same as multiplying by 10.)

sets.title: Multiply a decimal by a whole number

items.q: The grid shows 3 groups of 0.25 in two colors. What is 3 × 0.25?
items.e: The grid is 1 whole, so each square is 0.01 and 0.25 is 25 squares. 3 groups of 25 squares: 3 × 25 = 75 squares. 75 hundredths = 0.75, so 3 × 0.25 = 0.75. It is less than 1 because all the groups fit in one grid.

items.q: The grid shows 4 groups of 0.2 in two colors. What is 4 × 0.2?
items.e: The grid is 1 whole, so each square is 0.01 and 0.2 is 20 squares. 4 groups of 20 squares: 4 × 20 = 80 squares. 80 hundredths = 0.80 = 0.8, so 4 × 0.2 = 0.8. It is less than 1 because all the groups fit in one grid.

items.q: The grid shows 2 groups of 0.35 in two colors. What is 2 × 0.35?
items.e: The grid is 1 whole, so each square is 0.01 and 0.35 is 35 squares. 2 groups of 35 squares: 2 × 35 = 70 squares. 70 hundredths = 0.70 = 0.7, so 2 × 0.35 = 0.7. It is less than 1 because all the groups fit in one grid.

items.q: The grid shows 5 groups of 0.12 in two colors. What is 5 × 0.12?
items.e: The grid is 1 whole, so each square is 0.01 and 0.12 is 12 squares. 5 groups of 12 squares: 5 × 12 = 60 squares. 60 hundredths = 0.60 = 0.6, so 5 × 0.12 = 0.6. It is less than 1 because all the groups fit in one grid.
Estimate: 2.36 is about 2, and 4 × 2 = 8, so the answer is about 8. 2.36 has 2 decimal places, so the product has 2: 944 → 9.44.
Estimate: 3.08 is about 3, and 7 × 3 = 21, so the answer is about 21. 3.08 has 2 decimal places, so the product has 2: 2,156 → 21.56.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Estimate: 1.25 is about 1, and 6 × 1 = 6. Multiply as whole numbers: 6 × 125 = 750. 1.25 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 7.50 = 7.5.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Estimate: 4.67 is about 5, and 3 × 5 = 15. Multiply as whole numbers: 3 × 467 = 1,401. 4.67 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 14.01.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Estimate: 0.45 is less than 1, so the answer is less than 8. Multiply as whole numbers: 8 × 45 = 360. 0.45 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 3.60 = 3.6.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Estimate: 2.38 is about 2, and 5 × 2 = 10. Multiply as whole numbers: 5 × 238 = 1,190. 2.38 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 11.90 = 11.9.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Estimate: 0.7 is less than 1, so the answer is less than 9. Multiply as whole numbers: 9 × 7 = 63. 0.7 has 1 decimal place, so the product has it too: 6.3.

items.q: What is 4 × 3.6?
items.e: Estimate: 3.6 is about 4, and 4 × 4 = 16. Multiply as whole numbers: 4 × 36 = 144. 3.6 has 1 decimal place, so the product has it too: 14.4.

items.q: What is 7 × 0.08?
items.e: Estimate: 0.08 is less than 1, so the answer is less than 7. Multiply as whole numbers: 7 × 8 = 56. 0.08 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 0.56.

items.q: What is 6 × 12.5?
items.e: Estimate: 12.5 is about 12, and 6 × 12 = 72. Multiply as whole numbers: 6 × 125 = 750. 12.5 has 1 decimal place, so the product has it too: 75.0 = 75.

items.q: What is 2 × 5.06?
items.e: Estimate: 5.06 is about 5, and 2 × 5 = 10. Multiply as whole numbers: 2 × 506 = 1,012. 5.06 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 10.12.

items.q: What is 3 × 0.9?
items.e: Estimate: 0.9 is less than 1, so the answer is less than 3. Multiply as whole numbers: 3 × 9 = 27. 0.9 has 1 decimal place, so the product has it too: 2.7.

items.q: Without multiplying, which is true about 8 × 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 is less than 1, so 8 × 0.5 is less than 8 × 1 = 8. Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes it smaller. (8 × 0.5 is half of 8: 4.)

items.q: Which product is greater than 6?
items.e: Compare the other factor with 1. Only 1.2 is more than 1, so only 6 × 1.2 is more than 6 (it is 7.2). 6 × 1 is exactly 6, and 6 × 0.9 and 6 × 0.5 are less than 6.

items.q: What is 12 × 0.75?
items.e: Estimate: 0.75 is a bit less than 1, so the answer is a bit less than 12. Multiply as whole numbers: 12 × 75 = 900. 0.75 has 2 decimal places: 9.00 = 9.

items.q: What is 25 × 1.6?
items.e: Estimate: 1.6 is about 2, and 25 × 2 = 50, so the answer is a bit less than 50. Multiply as whole numbers: 25 × 16 = 400. 1.6 has 1 decimal place: 40.0 = 40.

sets.title: Multiply a decimal by a decimal

items.q: The dark squares show where the two parts overlap. What is 0.3 × 0.4?
items.e: The grid is 1 whole. 0.3 is 3 columns and 0.4 is 4 rows. The overlap is 3 × 4 = 12 squares, and each square is 0.01. So 0.3 × 0.4 = 0.12. Tenths × tenths = hundredths, so the product has 2 decimal places.

items.q: The dark squares show where the two parts overlap. What is 0.6 × 0.5?
items.e: The grid is 1 whole. 0.6 is 6 columns and 0.5 is 5 rows. The overlap is 6 × 5 = 30 squares, and each square is 0.01. So 0.6 × 0.5 = 0.30 = 0.3. Tenths × tenths = hundredths, so the product has 2 decimal places.

items.q: The dark squares show where the two parts overlap. What is 0.2 × 0.7?
items.e: The grid is 1 whole. 0.2 is 2 columns and 0.7 is 7 rows. The overlap is 2 × 7 = 14 squares, and each square is 0.01. So 0.2 × 0.7 = 0.14. Tenths × tenths = hundredths, so the product has 2 decimal places.

items.q: The dark squares show where the two parts overlap. What is 0.8 × 0.4?
items.e: The grid is 1 whole. 0.8 is 8 columns and 0.4 is 4 rows. The overlap is 8 × 4 = 32 squares, and each square is 0.01. So 0.8 × 0.4 = 0.32. Tenths × tenths = hundredths, so the product has 2 decimal places.

items.q: The dark squares show where the two parts overlap. What is 0.9 × 0.3?
items.e: The grid is 1 whole. 0.9 is 9 columns and 0.3 is 3 rows. The overlap is 9 × 3 = 27 squares, and each square is 0.01. So 0.9 × 0.3 = 0.27. Tenths × tenths = hundredths, so the product has 2 decimal places.

items.q: What is 1.2 × 0.3?
items.e: Estimate: 1.2 is about 1, and 1 × 0.3 = 0.3. Multiply as whole numbers: 12 × 3 = 36. Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so the product has 2: 0.36.

items.q: What is 2.5 × 0.4?
items.e: Estimate: 0.4 is a bit less than half, and half of 2.5 is 1.25. Multiply as whole numbers: 25 × 4 = 100. Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so the product has 2: 1.00 = 1.

items.q: What is 3.4 × 1.2?
items.e: Estimate: 3 × 1 = 3, so the answer is a bit more than 3. Multiply as whole numbers: 34 × 12 = 408. Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so the product has 2: 4.08. Keep the 0 in the tenths place: 4.08, not 4.8.

items.q: What is 1.5 × 2.6?
items.e: Estimate: 1.5 × 3 = 4.5, so a bit less than 4.5. Multiply as whole numbers: 15 × 26 = 390. Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so the product has 2: 3.90 = 3.9. (4.1 is 1.5 + 2.6, the sum, not the product.)
2.3 has 1 decimal place and 1.4 has 1 decimal place, so the product has 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places. Count 2 places from the right in 322: 3.22. Estimate to check: 2 × 1.5 = 3.
1.5 has 1 decimal place and 3.6 has 1 decimal place, so the product has 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places. Count 2 places from the right in 540: 5.40 = 5.4. Estimate to check: 1.5 × 4 = 6.
1.25 has 2 decimal places and 0.4 has 1 decimal place, so the product has 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places. Count 3 places from the right in 500: 0.500 = 0.5. Estimate to check: about 1 × 0.5 = 0.5.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 2.9 × 4.1?
items.e: Round each factor to the nearest whole number: 2.9 ≈ 3 and 4.1 ≈ 4. 3 × 4 = 12. (About 7 is the sum, 2.9 + 4.1.)

items.q: Without multiplying, which is the product of 4.8 × 3.1?
items.e: Estimate: 4.8 ≈ 5 and 3.1 ≈ 3, so the product is about 5 × 3 = 15. Only 14.88 is close to 15. (7.9 is the sum.)

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 6.2 × 0.48?
items.e: 6.2 ≈ 6 and 0.48 ≈ 0.5 (one half). Half of 6 is 3. The product is less than 6 because 0.48 is less than 1.

items.q: Which is true about 0.4 × 0.9?
items.e: 0.9 is less than 1, so 0.4 × 0.9 is less than 0.4. Check: 4 × 9 = 36, so 0.4 × 0.9 = 0.36, and 0.36 < 0.4.

items.q: Jack says 2.5 × 0.6 is greater than 2.5 because multiplying always makes a number bigger. Is he right?
items.e: 0.6 is less than 1, so 2.5 × 0.6 is less than 2.5. 25 × 6 = 150, and 2 decimal places give 1.50 = 1.5. Jack is not right: multiplying by a number less than 1 makes it smaller.

items.q: What is 0.5 × 0.12?
items.e: Estimate: 0.5 is half, so the answer is small, less than 0.12. Multiply as whole numbers: 5 × 12 = 60. 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places: 0.060 = 0.06. Keep the 0 of 60 when you count the places.

items.q: What is 0.2 × 0.35?
items.e: Estimate: 0.2 is a fifth, so the answer is small, less than 0.35. Multiply as whole numbers: 2 × 35 = 70. 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places: 0.070 = 0.07. Keep the 0 of 70 when you count the places.

items.q: 0.7 × 0.6 = 0.42. Why does the product have 2 decimal places?
items.e: 1 tenth of 1 tenth is 1 hundredth (one square of a hundredths grid). So tenths × tenths = hundredths: 7 tenths × 6 tenths = 42 hundredths = 0.42.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Estimate: 7.2 is between 6 and 9, so the answer is between 2 and 3. Divide as if there were no point: 72 ÷ 3 = 24. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend: 2.4. Check: 2.4 × 3 = 7.2.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Estimate: 0.84 is about 0.8, and 0.8 ÷ 4 = 0.2. Divide as if there were no point: 84 ÷ 4 = 21. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend: 0.21. 4 does not fit into 0 ones, so write 0 in the ones place. Check: 0.21 × 4 = 0.84.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Estimate: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Divide as if there were no point: 816 ÷ 4 = 204. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend: 2.04. 4 does not fit into 1 tenth, so write 0 in the tenths place. Check: 2.04 × 4 = 8.16.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Estimate: 5 ÷ 5 = 1. Divide as if there were no point: 525 ÷ 5 = 105. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend: 1.05. 5 does not fit into 2 tenths, so write 0 in the tenths place. Check: 1.05 × 5 = 5.25.

items.q: The quotient digits are written, but the point is missing. What is 9.36 ÷ 4?
items.e: Estimate: 9.36 is between 8 and 12, so the answer is between 2 and 3. Divide as if there were no point: 936 ÷ 4 = 234. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend: 2.34. Check: 2.34 × 4 = 9.36.

items.q: The quotient digits are written, but the point is missing. What is 1.35 ÷ 5?
items.e: Estimate: 1.35 is less than 5, so the quotient is less than 1. Divide as if there were no point: 135 ÷ 5 = 27. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend: 0.27. Check: 0.27 × 5 = 1.35.

items.q: The quotient digits are written, but the point is missing. What is 12.6 ÷ 3?
items.e: Estimate: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Divide as if there were no point: 126 ÷ 3 = 42. Put the point in the quotient straight above the point in the dividend: 4.2. Check: 4.2 × 3 = 12.6.

items.q: What is 4.5 ÷ 9?
items.e: Estimate: 4.5 is less than 9, so the answer is less than 1. 45 ÷ 9 = 5. Put the point above the point in 4.5: 4.5 ÷ 9 = 0.5. Check: 0.5 × 9 = 4.5. (2 is 9 ÷ 4.5, the wrong order.)

items.q: What is 6.3 ÷ 7?
items.e: Estimate: 6.3 is less than 7, so the answer is less than 1. 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Put the point above the point in 6.3: 0.9. Check: 0.9 × 7 = 6.3. (44.1 is 6.3 × 7.)

items.q: What is 4.8 ÷ 0.6?
items.e: Make the divisor a whole number: multiply both numbers by 10. 4.8 ÷ 0.6 = 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Check: 8 × 0.6 = 4.8. Dividing by a number less than 1 gives an answer bigger than 4.8.

items.q: What is 2.7 ÷ 0.3?
items.e: Make the divisor a whole number: multiply both numbers by 10. 2.7 ÷ 0.3 = 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Check: 9 × 0.3 = 2.7. Dividing by a number less than 1 gives an answer bigger than 2.7.
Make the divisor a whole number: multiply both numbers by 100. 0.56 ÷ 0.08 = 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Check: 7 × 0.08 = 0.56. Dividing by a number less than 1 gives an answer bigger than 0.56.

items.q: What is 1.2 ÷ 0.04?
items.e: Make the divisor a whole number: multiply both numbers by 100. 1.2 ÷ 0.04 = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. Check: 30 × 0.04 = 1.2. Dividing by a number less than 1 gives an answer bigger than 1.2.

items.q: What is 4 ÷ 0.2?
items.e: Make the divisor a whole number: multiply both numbers by 10. 4 ÷ 0.2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20. Check: 20 × 0.2 = 4. Dividing by a number less than 1 gives an answer bigger than 4.

items.q: What is 7.5 ÷ 2.5?
items.e: Make the divisor a whole number: multiply both numbers by 10. 7.5 ÷ 2.5 = 75 ÷ 25 = 3. Check: 3 × 2.5 = 7.5.

items.q: 3 ÷ 0.5 asks: how many halves are in 3? What is 3 ÷ 0.5?
items.e: Each whole has 2 halves, so 3 wholes have 3 × 2 = 6 halves. Or make the divisor whole: 3 ÷ 0.5 = 30 ÷ 5 = 6. (1.5 is 3 × 0.5.)

items.q: Which problem has the same answer as 3.6 ÷ 0.4?
items.e: Multiply both numbers by 10: 3.6 × 10 = 36 and 0.4 × 10 = 4. So 3.6 ÷ 0.4 = 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Move the point the same number of places in both numbers.

items.q: Which problem has the same answer as 1.75 ÷ 0.25?
items.e: 0.25 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100: 1.75 → 175 and 0.25 → 25. 1.75 ÷ 0.25 = 175 ÷ 25 = 7.

items.q: Without dividing, which is true about 9 ÷ 0.3?
items.e: 0.3 is less than 1, and many 0.3s fit into 9, so the answer is greater than 9. 9 ÷ 0.3 = 90 ÷ 3 = 30. (3 is 9 ÷ 3.)

items.q: 4.2 ÷ 6 = 0.7. Which product should equal 4.2 to check this?
items.e: Quotient × divisor = dividend. 0.7 × 6 = 4.2, so the answer is right.

sets.title: Word problems: money, length and capacity

items.q: A notebook costs $2.75. Ava buys 4 notebooks. How much does she pay?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 4 × $2.75. Estimate: $2.75 is about $3, and 4 × $3 = $12. 4 × 275 = 1,100, and 2 decimal places give $11.00. ($8.75 multiplies only the dollars: 4 × 2 + 0.75.)

items.q: A pack of 6 juice boxes costs $4.50. Each box costs the same. How much is one juice box?
items.e: Share $4.50 equally into 6 parts: 4.50 ÷ 6. Estimate: $4.50 is less than $6, so each box costs less than $1. 450 ÷ 6 = 75. Put the point above the point: $0.75. Check: 6 × $0.75 = $4.50.

items.q: Mia cuts a ribbon 3.6 m long into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: Divide: 3.6 ÷ 4. Estimate: 3.6 is a bit less than 4, so each piece is a bit less than 1 m. 36 ÷ 4 = 9, and the point goes above the point: 0.9 m. Check: 4 × 0.9 = 3.6.

items.q: A jug holds 2 L of lemonade. How many 0.25 L cups can be filled from it?
items.e: How many 0.25s are in 2? Divide: 2 ÷ 0.25 = 200 ÷ 25 = 8. Or: 4 cups make 1 L, so 2 L fill 8 cups. (0.5 is 2 × 0.25.)

items.q: Fabric costs $3.40 per meter. Omar buys 2.5 meters. How much does he pay?
items.e: Multiply: 2.5 × $3.40. Estimate: 2.5 × 3 = 7.5, so a bit more than $7.50. 25 × 34 = 850, and 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places give 8.500 = $8.50. ($5.90 is the sum.)

items.q: Zoe runs 2.4 km every day. How far does she run in 5 days?
items.e: Multiply: 5 × 2.4. Estimate: 5 × 2 = 10, so a bit more than 10 km. 5 × 24 = 120, and 1 decimal place gives 12.0 = 12 km.

items.q: A bag holds 4.5 kg of rice. A family uses 0.4 of the bag in a week. How much rice is that?
items.e: “0.4 of” means multiply: 0.4 × 4.5. Estimate: 0.4 is a bit less than half, and half of 4.5 is about 2. 4 × 45 = 180, and 2 decimal places give 1.80 = 1.8 kg. The answer is less than 4.5 because 0.4 < 1.

items.q: A recipe needs 0.75 cup of flour. Eli makes 3 batches. How much flour does he need?
items.e: Multiply: 3 × 0.75. Estimate: 0.75 is about 1, so a bit less than 3 cups. 3 × 75 = 225, and 2 decimal places give 2.25 cups. (3.75 adds 3 instead of multiplying.)

items.q: Five friends share $12 equally. How much does each friend get?
items.e: Divide: $12 ÷ 5. Estimate: $10 ÷ 5 = $2, so a bit more than $2. Write 12 as 12.00: 1,200 ÷ 5 = 240, so each friend gets $2.40. Check: 5 × $2.40 = $12.00.

items.q: Pencils cost $0.35 each. Sam has $2.80. How many pencils can he buy?
items.e: How many $0.35s are in $2.80? Divide: 2.80 ÷ 0.35 = 280 ÷ 35 = 8. Check: 8 × $0.35 = $2.80. (0.98 is 2.80 × 0.35: multiplying instead of dividing.)

items.q: How many 0.5 L bottles can be filled with 6 L of water?
items.e: Each liter fills 2 bottles of 0.5 L. 6 ÷ 0.5 = 60 ÷ 5 = 12. (3 is 6 × 0.5.)

items.q: Nora has a board 2.5 m long. She cuts it into pieces 0.5 m long. How many pieces does she get?
A garden is 3.5 m long and 2.4 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 3.5 × 2.4. Estimate: 3.5 × 2 = 7, so a bit more than 7. 35 × 24 = 840, and 2 decimal places give 8.40 = 8.4 m². (11.8 is the perimeter.)

items.q: Maya multiplies 4.2 × 3.8 and gets 159.6. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 4.2 ≈ 4 and 3.8 ≈ 4, so the product is about 16. 159.6 is 10 times too big: the point is in the wrong place. The answer is 15.96.

items.q: Grapes cost $2.40 per pound. How much do 1.5 pounds of grapes cost?
items.e: Multiply: 1.5 × $2.40. Estimate: half of 2.40 is 1.20, so 1.5 pounds cost about $2.40 + $1.20. 15 × 24 = 360, and 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places give $3.60. ($3.90 is the sum.)

items.q: Emma spends $18.60 on 6 books. Each book costs the same. How much does one book cost?
items.e: Divide: 18.60 ÷ 6. Estimate: 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so about $3. 1,860 ÷ 6 = 310, so one book costs $3.10. Check: 6 × $3.10 = $18.60.

items.q: A pitcher holds 1.8 L of juice. It is poured equally into 6 glasses. How much juice is in each glass?
items.e: Divide: 1.8 ÷ 6. Estimate: 1.8 is less than 6, so each glass gets less than 1 L. 18 ÷ 6 = 3, and the point goes above the point: 0.3 L. Check: 6 × 0.3 = 1.8.

items.q: A nickel is 1.95 mm thick. How tall is a stack of 10 nickels?
items.e: Multiply by 10: the point moves 1 place to the right. 1.95 × 10 = 19.5 mm. Check: 10 × 2 = 20, so about 20 mm.

items.q: A sheet of paper is 0.1 mm thick. How thick is a stack of 500 sheets?
items.e: Multiply: 500 × 0.1. Multiplying by 0.1 is dividing by 10: 500 ÷ 10 = 50 mm.

items.q: Ben walks 0.8 km to school each morning and the same way home. How far does he walk in 5 school days?
items.e: Each day: 0.8 + 0.8 = 1.6 km. In 5 days: 5 × 1.6 = 8 km. (4 km counts only the walk to school.)
